text:
Them 1: Morning everyone, shall we get started? I am Dana, head of marketing at Harbour Freight Partners.
You: Morning Dana, great to meet properly. I am the project lead on our side, and I have Sam from design joining shortly.
Them 1: Wonderful. Let us start with the brief, did you manage to read through it?
You: Yes, I did, and I have a few questions, mainly about the case study library.
Them 1: Go ahead, that is the part everybody cares about most internally.
You: How many case studies do you expect at launch, and who supplies the content?
Them 1: About twelve at launch, and we will supply the text and photos in a shared folder.
You: Good. I'll send you a content template after this call so everything arrives in the same shape.
Them 1: That would really help, thank you.
You: Okay. Let me just share my screen so we can look at the plan together.
Them 1: Sure, I can see it now, give me a second to find the right window.
You: So design sign-off week two, build weeks three to five, launch end of week six. Does that match your expectation?
Them 1: Yes, though our CEO wants to see the homepage early, ideally before the end of the first week.
You: Okay. We'll share the first homepage concept by Thursday so your CEO can react to it.
You: Next, navigation. We suggest five top level items: services, case studies, about, news and contact.
Them 1: We have a lot of services, will five items be enough, or will it feel crowded?
You: Services becomes a mega menu, so the detail lives one level down and the top bar stays clean.
Them 1: I like that. Our current site has fourteen items and nobody can find anything.
You: That is exactly the problem we want to remove. Fewer choices, clearer labels.
Them 1: Our operations people will also want a page for each depot, with opening hours and a map.
You: That is easy to add as a template, we can generate the depot pages from a spreadsheet.
Them 1: Even better, the spreadsheet already exists and somebody keeps it up to date, thankfully.
Them 1: Brilliant. What about the quote request form, who builds the connection to our CRM?
You: We do. I'll check with our developer how the CRM connection works and let you know what we find.
Them 1: Great, that is the part my sales director worries about.
You: If it breaks I'll call them straight away, they have always been quick to fix things on the integration side.
Them 1: Good to know. And budget, the fixed fee covers three rounds of design revisions, correct?
You: Correct. After the third round extra revisions are billed hourly, but most clients never need that.
Them 1: Fine. One more thing, our legal team needs to approve the privacy wording on the form.
You: I'll think about it and come back with a proposal for how we handle the approval step.
Them 1: That works. They are slow, so the sooner the better.
You: Understood. I'll put together a one page plan for the legal review and send it to you on Friday.
Them 1: Perfect. Sam, welcome, we were just talking about the homepage concept.
You: Sam, we agreed to show the first concept on Thursday, can you make that work?
Them 1: Hi both, sorry I am late. Thursday is fine, I will bring two directions.
You: Good. Dana, I'll schedule a weekly check in so nothing drifts.
Them 1: I like that, Monday mornings are best for me.
You: Then we are set. I'll update the timeline document and share it with you both after this call.
Them 1: Thank you, that is helpful. Anything else for today?
Them 1: No, I think that covers it, thank you both.
You: Thanks all, speak Monday.
